messages:
maria-cs: Customer ACME-Retail reporting repeated 403s when sending embeddings+generate in the same HTTP/2 request. They say the token is present client-side but server logs show missing scopes. Key prefix: rk_XXX (they shared a redacted key). Error: `403 Missing inference permission` after embeddings call.

eli-engineering: Can you paste the minimal repro curl and the raw headers? Also which client library/version?

maria-cs: Repro (customer used curl with --http2):
```
curl -v --http2 https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "User-Agent: acme-integration/1.2" \
  --data '{"input": "test"}' \
  --header "Token-Trailer: rk_XXX" \n  # they put the token as a trailer via their proxy
```
They said their edge proxy appends the token as an HTTP/2 trailer (was trying to avoid exposing Authorization in access logs).

jordan-logs: Pasted server-side excerpt (sanitized):
```
2026-03-17T14:22:10Z INFO request id=abc123 path=/v1/embeddings auth=none scopes=[] client=10.2.1.5
2026-03-17T14:22:10Z WARN auth: no token found in headers or auth metadata
```
You can see the request hit us but we didn't observe an Authorization header or token metadata.

sam-infra: Quick theory: our edge gateway (haproxy/nginx) is configured to drop HTTP/2 trailers by default, or the internal HTTP/2->HTTP/1.1 translation strips them. Trailers are not reliably preserved across our proxy chain. Using trailers for auth is a risky pattern.

eli-engineering: Agreed. Two immediate options: 1) tell customer to put the key in `Authorization: Bearer <key>` or `x-api-key` header (preferred), or 2) adjust our gateway mapping to forward trailers into a header (`preserve_trailers`/`http2-copy-trailers`), but that needs infra review.

ci-deploy-bot: deploy #edge-proxy-config v2026.3.17 started by @sam-infra :rocket:

sam-infra: I'll test a quick config on staging to demonstrate. If we do a mapping we should also normalize into `x-forwarded-token` and run a short regression.

maria-cs: Customer tried switching to `Authorization: Bearer <redacted>` and they immediately got a 200 for both embeddings and generate. They want to know if this is a bug on our side or expected behavior.

eli-engineering: It's expected behavior given current proxy chain: trailers may be dropped. Not a scope check bug — server never saw the token, so scopes looked empty and we returned 403. We should document "do not use HTTP/2 trailers for auth" in our integration guide.

tess-support: Can we escalate docs + email the customer steps and recommended headers? Also advise rotating the key since it traveled in an unusual header/trailer. @maria-cs please confirm org id and that they rotated.

maria-cs: Confirmed org=acme-retail-prod, customer rotated key and tested. They accepted guidance to use `Authorization` header.

eli-engineering: I'll open a short infra ticket to evaluate preserving trailers for internal customers, but we shouldn't rely on it. Also adding a note to our onboarding quickstart.

sam-infra: Staging test showed mapping trailers->header works, but it's flaky with some HTTP/2 clients; not recommended as primary auth path.

jordan-logs: Added a server-side debug log to better call out missing token versus bad scope to help future triage (will be noisy for an hour).

tess-support: Thanks all. I'll send the customer summary and mark the case resolved once they confirm stability. :white_check_mark:

maria-cs: Customer confirmed stable after rotation and header change. Closing thread. :thumbsup:
